question: Oil Change International’s research illustrates fuel supplies to Israel in the context of the genocide in Gaza and paints a picture of the human rights violations committed by oil companies. It highlights how 54 % of shipments took place after the International Court of Justice’s 26/01/2024 recommendation on the obligation to prevent genocide.

ENI exported 30 000 tons of crude oil from the Val D’Agri Center in Italy in the year 2024. In the recent case of Taranto, workers, trade unions and activists have denounced the fact that these shipments are still fuelling the Israeli war machine. Furthermore, ENI has a partnership with the Israeli group Delek, which the UN has blacklisted for its operations in the occupied Palestinian territories. 1.
What monitoring tools does the Commission use to investigate possible violations of EU human rights standards by ENI in its supplies to Israel?
What measures is the Commission taking to ensure that oil multinationals respect EU Directive 2024/17601 regarding the assessment of human rights impacts in conflict zones and environmental rights?

Considering the revision of Article 2 of the EU-Israel Agreement supported by several Member States, what ‘appropriate measures’ under Article 79 will the Commission propose to ensure compliance with human rights obligations and the Genocide Convention?
OJ L, 2024/1760, 5.7.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/1760/oj.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.1.2026) Since the onset of the Israel/Hamas conflict, the EU recognised Israel’s right to defend itself, but consistently urged Israel to do so in line with international law, international human rights law and international humanitarian law.

The EU has also clearly emphasised its expectation that Israel complies with rulings of international courts, including the order of the International Court of Justice of 26 January 20241. This order neither addresses nor sets out any obligations for third states and organisations.

Further to the findings of the review launched by the High Representative/Vice-President in May 2025 on Israel's compliance with its human rights obligations, which are an essential element of the EU-Israel Association Agreement2 by virtue of its Article 2, and in response to the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Gaza, the President of the Commission announced in her State of the Union 2025 address3 in September 2025 a package of measures designated to exercise pressure on Israel.

Those proposals are currently discussed in the Council. Regarding the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD)4, Member States have until July 2029 to ensure its transposition into national law and to designate their respective supervisory authorities5.
The Commission will issue guidelines on the application of the CSDDD, and it will set up the European Network of Supervisory Authorities to coordinate their enforcement efforts.
